source.title: Some Open Questions on Anti-de Sitter Geometry

accepted.question_text: Let n = 2m + 1 > 3, and let M = Γ\AdS^n be a compact anti-de Sitter manifold where Γ is a discrete group of isometries acting properly discontinuously on AdS^n. Must Γ, up to conjugacy in the isometry group, be a uniform lattice in U(m,1)?
accepted.context_brief: Compact AdS rigidity in odd dimension > 3

evidence.quote: Question 2.1. Suppose n = 2m + 1 > 3. Let M = Γ\AdSn be a compact AdS manifold, where Γ is a discrete group of isometries acting properly discontinuously on AdSn. Is Γ necessarily a uniform lattice in U(m, 1) (up to conjugacy)?

accepted.question_text: Fix a closed hyperbolic surface S of genus at least 2. Let Adm(S) be the space of admissible pairs (j,ρ) of representations π_1(S) → PSL_2(R) with j Fuchsian and such that the induced action on AdS^3 is properly discontinuous and cocompact. How many connected components does Adm(S) have, and what is its topology?
accepted.context_brief: Topology of the admissible representation space

evidence.quote: Question 2.2. How many connected components does the space Adm(S) have? What is its topology?

accepted.question_text: Which numerical values can occur as the volume of a compact anti-de Sitter 3-manifold? For a quotient Γ\AdS^3 coming from an admissible pair (j,ρ) in Adm(S), does the volume depend only on the Euler number of ρ, or can it vary within a fixed connected component of Adm(S)?
accepted.context_brief: Volumes of compact AdS 3-manifolds

evidence.quote: Question 2.3. Which values can the volume of a compact AdS 3-manifold take? For Γ = {(j(γ), ρ(γ)) : γ ∈ π1(S)} with (j, ρ) ∈ Adm(S), does the volume of Γ\AdS3 depend only on the Euler number of ρ, or does it vary when (j, ρ) varies in a given connected component of Adm(S)?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, let M = S × R, and let l_- and l_+ be two measured laminations on S that fill S. Is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M whose convex-core boundary has measured bending laminations exactly l_- and l_+?
accepted.context_brief: Bending laminations determine GHMC AdS structure

evidence.quote: Question 3.1. If l− and l+ are two measured laminations which fill S, is there a unique GHMC AdS structure h on M such that l− and l+ are the measured bending laminations of the boundary of the convex core?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, and let l_- and l_+ be measured laminations that fill S. If E_l(l_-) and E_l(l_+) denote the corresponding right earthquakes of Teichmüller space T, does the composition E_l(l_-) ◦ E_l(l_+) have a unique fixed point in T?
accepted.context_brief: Uniqueness of earthquake fixed points

evidence.quote: Question 3.2. Let l−, l+ be two measured laminations which fill S. Does the composition El(l−) ◦ El(l+) have a unique fixed point in T ?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, let T be its Teichmüller space, and let m_- and m_+ be two points of T. Is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M = S × R such that the induced hyperbolic metrics on the two connected components of the boundary of the convex core are m_- and m_+?
accepted.context_brief: Convex-core boundary metrics determine GHMC structure

evidence.quote: Question 3.3. Let m−, m+ ∈ T . Is there a unique h ∈ GH such that the induced metric on the two connected components of the boundary of the convex core are m− and m+?

accepted.question_text: For a closed surface S of genus at least 2 with Teichmüller space T, define U : T × T → T × T by sending a pair of hyperbolic metrics (h_l,h_r) to the midpoints (h_-,h_+) of the left and right earthquake paths from h_l to h_r. Is U a homeomorphism?
accepted.context_brief: Earthquake midpoint map

evidence.quote: Question 3.4. Is U a homeomorphism?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, and let h_- and h_+ be two metrics on S with curvature strictly less than -1 everywhere. Is there a unique anti-de Sitter 3-manifold N with smooth, space-like, strictly convex boundary such that the induced metrics on the two connected components of ∂N are h_- and h_+, respectively?
accepted.context_brief: Smooth strictly convex AdS boundary metrics

evidence.quote: Question 3.5. Let h−, h+ be two metrics on S with curvature κ < −1. Is there a unique AdS manifold N with smooth, space-like, strictly convex boundary such that the induced metrics on the two connected components of ∂N are equal respectively to h− and h+?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2, and let h_- and h_+ be hyperbolic metrics on S with cone singularities whose cone angles are greater than 2π. Is there a unique anti-de Sitter manifold with convex polyhedral boundary whose induced boundary metrics are h_- and h_+?
accepted.context_brief: Polyhedral AdS boundaries with prescribed cone metrics

evidence.quote: Question 3.6. Let h−, h+ be two hyperbolic metrics on S with cone singularities of angle larger than 2π. Is there a unique AdS manifold with convex, polyhedral boundary for which the induced metric on the boundary is given by h− and h+?

accepted.question_text: For a globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold M = S × R with closed surface S of genus at least 2, is either the total volume V(M) or the convex-core volume V(C(M)) quasi-equivalent to a natural distance, such as the Teichmüller distance or the Weil–Petersson distance, between the induced metrics on the convex-core boundary or between the left and right hyperbolic metrics?
accepted.context_brief: Volume versus geometric distance

evidence.quote: Question 4.1. Is V (M) or V (C(M)) quasi-equivalent to a distance (for instance the Teichmüller distance, or the Weil–Petersson distance) between the induced metrics on the boundary of the convex core, or between the left and right hyperbolic metrics?

accepted.question_text: Is the total volume V(M) of a globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold minimized at the Fuchsian locus?
accepted.context_brief: Volume minimum at Fuchsian locus

evidence.quote: Question 4.2. Is V (M) minimal at the Fuchsian locus?

accepted.question_text: Fix a closed surface S and a hyperbolic metric h_l on S. For each h_r in Teichmüller space T, let M(h_l,h_r) be the unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold with left and right hyperbolic metrics h_l and h_r. Are the functions h_r ↦ V(M(h_l,h_r)) and h_r ↦ V(C(M(h_l,h_r))) convex? Are they proper? Does each have a unique minimum at h_l?
accepted.context_brief: Convexity and properness of AdS volume functions

evidence.quote: Question 4.3. Are these functions convex? Are they proper? Do they have a unique minimum at hl?

accepted.question_text: Let n ≥ 1. Are the Cauchy hypersurfaces of every globally hyperbolic maximal compact manifold locally modeled on AdS^(n+1) diffeomorphic to a quotient of H^p × H^q by a uniform lattice in SO(1,p) × SO(1,q), where p + q = n?
accepted.context_brief: Topology of higher-dimensional GHMC AdS Cauchy surfaces

evidence.quote: Question 5.1. Prove that the Cauchy surfaces of a GHMC manifold locally modeled on AdSn+1 are diffeomorphic to the quotient of Hp × Hq by a uniform lattice of SO(1, p) × SO(1, q) with p + q = n.

accepted.question_text: Is every globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold a deformation of a GH-standard anti-de Sitter manifold, namely one obtained from a quotient Γ\Ω with Γ contained in SO(1,p) × SO(1,q) ⊂ SO(2,n) for some p + q = n?
accepted.context_brief: Deformation from GH-standard examples

evidence.quote: Question 5.2. Is every GHMC AdS manifold a deformation of a GH-standard AdS manifold?

accepted.question_text: For a globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter manifold of arbitrary dimension, does the past of the convex core always admit a K-time, meaning a time function whose level sets have constant Gauss–Killing–Kronecker–Lipschitz curvature ranging in (-∞,0)?
accepted.context_brief: Existence of K-time in arbitrary dimension

evidence.quote: Question 6.1. Does the past of the convex core of a GHMC AdS manifold (of arbitrary dimension) always possess a K-time?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter 3-manifold with massive particles, meaning cone singularities of angle less than π along timelike lines. Is there a unique maximal spacelike surface in M that is orthogonal to the particle worldlines?
accepted.context_brief: Maximal surfaces with particles

evidence.quote: Question 6.2. Is there a unique maximal space-like surface in M orthogonal to the particles?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a closed surface with marked points x_1, ..., x_n and cone angles θ_1, ..., θ_n in (0,π). If h and h' are hyperbolic metrics on S with cone singularities of angle θ_i at x_i, is there a unique minimal Lagrangian diffeomorphism from (S,h) to (S,h') that is isotopic to the identity and fixes each x_i?
accepted.context_brief: Minimal Lagrangian maps between cone metrics

evidence.quote: Question 6.3. Let S be a closed surface. Choose x1, · · · , xn ∈ S and θ1, · · · , θn ∈ (0, π), and let h, h′ be two hyperbolic metrics on S with cone singularities of angle θi at xi. Is there a unique minimal Lagrangian diffeomorphism isotopic to the identity fixing the xi between (S, h) and (S, h′)?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter manifold with particles of cone angle less than π. Does M admit a unique constant-mean-curvature time function whose level surfaces are all orthogonal to the singularities?
accepted.context_brief: CMC time with cone singularities

evidence.quote: Question 6.4. Does M admit a unique CMC time with each surface of constant time orthogonal to the singularities?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a globally hyperbolic anti-de Sitter manifold with particles of cone angle less than π. Does the past of the convex core, and likewise the future, admit a unique foliation by surfaces of constant Gauss curvature?
accepted.context_brief: Constant Gauss curvature foliations with particles

evidence.quote: Question 6.5. Does the past (resp. future) of the convex core of M have a unique foliation by constant Gauss curvature?

accepted.question_text: Let S be the interior of a compact surface with boundary, let h_l and h_r be complete convex cocompact hyperbolic metrics on S, and let ρ_l,ρ_r : π_1(S) → PSL_2(R) be the corresponding holonomies. How can one detect geometrically whether the action of (ρ_l,ρ_r)(π_1(S)) on AdS^3 is proper or non-proper from the hyperbolic metrics on the boundary components of the convex core or from the bending laminations?
accepted.context_brief: Geometric detection of proper actions on AdS^3

evidence.quote: Question 7.1. Let hl, hr ∈ TS and let ρl, ρr : π1(S) → PSL2(R) be the corresponding holonomies. How can one read the properness or non-properness of the action of (ρl, ρr)(π1(S)) on AdS3: • on the hyperbolic metrics of the boundary components of the convex core? • on the bending laminations?

accepted.question_text: For anti-de Sitter 3-manifolds with interacting particles, where the singular set is allowed to be a graph and cone angles are less than 2π, does the local parameterization proposed by sequences of pairs of hyperbolic cone metrics extend to a global parameterization, or are extra conditions on the parameter data necessary?
accepted.context_brief: Global parameterization with interacting particles

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to understand whether this parameterization is global, or whether some additional condition on the parameterization data must be imposed to obtain a global parameterization.

accepted.question_text: Let GH be the space of globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structures on a closed surface bundle M = S × R. Using the maximal-surface parameterization GH ≅ T*Teich(S) and the left-right parameterization GH ≅ Teich(S) × Teich(S), one gets a map φ : T*Teich(S) → Teich(S) × Teich(S). Is φ symplectic, in the sense that the pullback of the difference of the Weil–Petersson symplectic forms equals, up to a constant, the canonical cotangent symplectic structure on T*Teich(S)?
accepted.context_brief: Symplecticity of the maximal-surface parameterization

evidence.quote: Question 8.1. Is φ symplectic, that is, is the pull-back by φ of the difference of the Weil–Petersson symplectic forms on the two factors in the image equal (up to a constant) to the cotangent symplectic structure on T∗T ?

accepted.question_text: Let ψ : S^1 → S^1 be an orientation-preserving quasisymmetric homeomorphism. Is there a unique quasiconformal harmonic diffeomorphism φ : H^2 → H^2 that extends continuously to the boundary at infinity and restricts there to ψ?
accepted.context_brief: Harmonic extension of quasisymmetric circle maps

evidence.quote: Question 8.2. Let ψ : S1 → S1 be an orientation-preserving quasi-symmetric homeomorphism. Is there a unique quasi-conformal harmonic diffeomorphism φ : H2 → H2 such that φ extends continuously at infinity and its restriction to the boundary at infinity of H2 is ψ?

accepted.question_text: Let Λ ⊂ ∂_∞AdS^3 be the graph of a quasisymmetric homeomorphism RP^1 → RP^1, and let D be the domain of dependence defined by Λ. Is there a unique foliation of D by spacelike constant-mean-curvature surfaces with bounded principal curvatures and boundary at infinity Λ?
accepted.context_brief: CMC foliations with prescribed boundary at infinity

evidence.quote: Question 8.3. Is there a unique foliation of D by space-like, constant mean curvature surfaces with bounded principal curvature and boundary at infinity Λ?

accepted.question_text: Let Λ ⊂ ∂_∞AdS^3 be the graph of a quasisymmetric homeomorphism RP^1 → RP^1, let C be its convex hull, and let D be the corresponding domain of dependence. Is there a unique foliation of D \ C by spacelike surfaces of constant Gauss curvature whose principal curvatures stay bounded?
accepted.context_brief: Gauss-curvature foliations outside the convex hull

evidence.quote: Question 8.4. Is there a unique foliation of D r C by space-like, constant Gauss curvature surfaces with bounded principal curvatures?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a closed surface of genus at least 2 and M = S × R. If l_- and l_+ are weighted multicurves on S that fill S, is there a unique globally hyperbolic maximal compact anti-de Sitter structure h on M whose convex-core boundary has measured bending laminations l_- and l_+?
accepted.context_brief: Uniqueness for rational bending data

evidence.quote: Question 9.1. If l− and l+ are weighted multi-curves which fill S, is there a unique GHMC AdS structure h on M such that l− and l+ are the measured bending laminations of the boundary of the convex core?

accepted.question_text: Let N be a closed anti-de Sitter 3-manifold with tachyon singularities along a link, where the holonomy around each singular component is a Lorentz boost and the corresponding boost magnitude (the tachyon mass) is fixed. Is the anti-de Sitter geometry of N locally rigid relative to those tachyon masses?
accepted.context_brief: Local rigidity of tachyon manifolds

evidence.quote: Question 9.2. Let N be a closed AdS manifold with tachyons, so that the singular locus is a link. Is the AdS geometry of N rigid relative to the tachyon mass?

accepted.question_text: Let N be a closed anti-de Sitter 3-manifold with tachyon singularities along a link, and assume that the complement of the singular locus is atoroidal. Under this extra topological hypothesis, is the anti-de Sitter geometry of N rigid relative to the tachyon masses?
accepted.context_brief: Rigidity with atoroidal singular-link complement

evidence.quote: Question 9.3. Let N be a closed AdS manifold with tachyons, so that the singular locus is a link. Further, assume that the complement of the singular locus is atoroidal. Is the AdS geometry of N rigid relative to the tachyon mass?

accepted.question_text: Let N be a closed 3-manifold with a nonsingular anti-de Sitter structure, and let Σ be a link in N. Do there exist nearby anti-de Sitter structures on N with tachyon singularities along Σ? What topological or geometric conditions on the pair (N,Σ) are necessary for such deformations to exist?
accepted.context_brief: Introducing tachyons along a chosen link

evidence.quote: Question 9.5. Let N be a closed 3-manifold with a non-singular AdS structure and let Σ be a link in N. Do there exist nearby AdS structures with tachyon singularities along Σ? What topological conditions on (N, Σ) are needed to have such deformations? Geometric conditions?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a closed surface and let ρ_l,ρ_r : π_1(S) → PSL_2(C) be quasi-Fuchsian representations. Does there exist a ρ_l-ρ_r-equivariant spacelike embedding of the universal cover S~ into the complex anti-de Sitter space X_C = O(4,C)/O(3,C)? If such an embedding exists, can one choose one of constant curvature?
accepted.context_brief: Equivariant spacelike surfaces in complex AdS space

evidence.quote: Question 10.1. Given two quasi-Fuchsian representations of π1(S) into PSL2(C), is there an equivariant space-like embedding Se → XC? In this case, may we find such an embedding of constant curvature?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a closed surface and let ρ_l,ρ_r : π_1(S) → PSL_2(C) be quasi-Fuchsian representations. Is there a maximal domain in the complex anti-de Sitter space X_C on which the group (ρ_l,ρ_r)(π_1(S)) acts properly discontinuously, and if so, what is the topology of the quotient?
accepted.context_brief: Proper domains for quasi-Fuchsian complex AdS actions

evidence.quote: Question 10.2. Given two quasi-Fuchsian representations ρl, ρr of π1(S) into PSL2(C), is there a (maximal) domain of XC where the action of the group (ρl, ρr)(π1(S)) ⊂ PSL2(C) × PSL2(C) is properly discontinuous? What is the topology of the corresponding quotient?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a hyperbolic 3-manifold and let ρ_l,ρ_r : π_1(M) → PSL_2(C) be convex cocompact representations. Is there a maximal domain in the complex anti-de Sitter space X_C on which (ρ_l,ρ_r)(π_1(M)) acts properly discontinuously? What is the topology of the quotient, and how can one recognize geometrically whether the action is proper or non-proper?
accepted.context_brief: Proper domains for convex cocompact complex AdS actions

evidence.quote: Question 10.3. Let M be a hyperbolic 3-manifold and let (ρl, ρr) be a pair of convex cocompact representations of π1(M) into PSL2(C). Is there a (maximal) domain of XC where the action of the group (ρl, ρr)(π1(M)) ⊂ PSL2(C) × PSL2(C) is properly discontinuous? What is the topology of the corresponding quotient? How can one read geometrically the properness or non-properness of the action of (ρl, ρr)(π1(M)) ⊂ PSL2(C) × PSL2(C) on XC?

needs_review.question_text_raw: It would be interesting to understand whether there is a good relation between the width and the Teichmüller (or Weil–Petersson) distance ... A natural question is whether a bound on the Teichmüller distance implies a bound on ml(hl, hr).

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to understand whether there is a good relation between this width and the Teichmüller (or Weil–Petersson) distance between the left and right hyperbolic metrics of M. ... A natural question is whether a bound on the Teichmüller distance implies a bound on ml(hl, hr).

needs_review.question_text_raw: One could imagine that the space of metrics of this type with n particles of fixed angle on S × R ... is parameterized by the product of two copies of the Teichmüller space of S with n marked points. ... it might then be possible to obtain ... a version of Thurston's earthquake theorem ... A further step ... angles less than 2π and the particles are allowed to interact.

evidence.quote: One could imagine that the space of metrics of this type with n particles of fixed angle on S × R, where S is now the interior of a compact surface with non-empty boundary, is parameterized by the product of two copies of the Teichmüller space of S with n marked points. ... Using the argument developed by Mess [Mes07], it might then be possible to obtain as a corollary a version of Thurston’s earthquake theorem ... A further step in this direction would be to extend to multi-black holes the (still partial) results known for globally hyperbolic manifolds when the angles are only less than 2π and the particles are allowed to interact
